structural_boundary: No complete fces.semantic-review-dossier.v1, governed claim set or required-question IDs supplied. This is an independent report-bound extraction review, not kernel-admissible semantic findings and not host admission.
scope: All43 source bodies and connector receipt contents integrity-checked; all43 evidence spans reviewed with focused surrounding high-risk source context. Not an exhaustive review of every source line, route, dependency, or runtime.

review_units.label: Desktop → server → engine
review_units.rationale: The desktop imports and awaits startEmbeddedServer, while embedded startup binds HTTP first and conditionally launches a managed engine when configured without an external URL. Cleanup calls task-recovery checkpoint before engine disposal. This is a managed path, not proof every startup spawns an engine or of installed readiness.

review_units.label: Actual OpenCode dependency
review_units.rationale: Full package lines 15 and 56 plus v1 launch lines 150-191 and the v2 module establish a real source integration beyond the prior metadata advertisement. OW04 is an inadequate locator, and the v2 module labels itself a prototype. No exact installed engine, resolved SDK lock or successful binary execution is established.

review_units.label: Engine generations
review_units.rationale: The captured pool coalesces rollovers behind a drain, probes standby health before promotion and retains primary on that probe failure. It can still promote after prepareStandby fails and can abort inactive draining sessions. This is source branch behavior, not a proof of provider-ready promotion or lossless rollover.

review_units.label: Persistence
review_units.rationale: The retained implementations open Bun/Node SQLite, upsert workspace JSON and serialize registry mutation through a process-local queue with private temporary files plus rename. The report correctly does not infer distributed ownership/fencing from those mechanisms.

review_units.label: Local interrupted-task recovery
review_units.rationale: The full recovery module only reloads running records, checks matching local workspace/current user turn and blocked/delegated state, caps recovered work at two, persists claimed state before send, and skips that claimed record on restart. It is single-server coordination, not a cross-process exactly-once effect ledger; the report preserves that limit.

review_units.label: Server access and permissions
review_units.rationale: Host/client/policy routing and effective permission summaries are present. The non-owner wording must distinguish viewer restrictions from collaborators explicitly allowed to reply. Effective-permissions summarizes rules/provenance; it does not enforce every route.

review_units.label: Managed tool checks
review_units.rationale: The captured plugin registers pre-tool and model hooks; the shared client maps named actions and syncs unknown/read-only tools, refusing missing policy URL/token and applying a 15-second request timeout. The policy evaluator and complete adapter/plugin installation coverage remain unverified; this does not prove every tool in both generations reaches an enforcing policy decision.

review_units.label: Skills and MCP
review_units.rationale: The full source parses project/global skill metadata, validates names, and shows selected skill mutation routes with write/scope/approval/audit/reload steps. MCP add/remove/enable uses runtime configuration storage. Approval requests do not imply an interactive human prompt in every configured mode.

review_units.label: Remembered thread approval
review_units.rationale: Stored grants are scoped by workspace/session and can replay an always response for a matching engine ask. The report proposes, rather than claims, revocation and unrelated-child protection. Full policy/identity revocation enforcement remains outside these grant functions.

review_units.label: Native remote control
review_units.rationale: The desktop HTTP bridge binds random loopback, exempts health from bearer checks, and wires HTTP disconnect to browser/WebMCP cancellation. The mailbox is in-memory, expires after five seconds and tracks delivery. Neither cancellation nor expiry proves reversal of delivered effects; private discovery file protections beyond the shown write are unverified.

review_units.label: Browser operations
review_units.rationale: The captured act path checks supplied conversation/tab ownership, visibility, observation identity, approval, navigation/revision and coordinate-image digest; it consumes the observation and returns unverified/nonretryable after input. Password/OTP restrictions are selective. Caller session authority, injected callbacks, frame/canvas handling and complete secret filtering are not proved by this helper.

review_units.label: WebMCP frame rights
review_units.rationale: Native lineage, explicit permissions-policy denial and cross-origin delegation checks are present. Missing/stale final isolated policy can produce allowed:true with originKeyed:false. With the consuming caller absent, the report cannot claim all navigated/stale frames fail end-to-end.

review_units.label: Automation contracts
review_units.rationale: The schema declares idempotent/durable capabilities and the validator checks receipt identity, contiguous sequence and duplicate event keys. The report correctly labels these as contracts rather than evidence every concrete adapter fulfills them.

review_units.label: EE cloud execution
review_units.rationale: Repeated model/owner-authority checks, previous-worker mismatch refusal and abort-plus-idle observation branches exist. The receipt boundary only awaits an injected onAdmitted callback; its persistent implementation is absent. Thread-idle observation is not whole-tree process exit or independent deliverable acceptance.

review_units.label: EE authentication and entitlement
review_units.rationale: The captured auth path checks verified token scope/use/resource, grant-or-session liveness and organization membership; liveness errors receive distinct failures. Entitlement gating can be disabled. Grant checks delegate to cache.auth.grant, and cache freshness/invalidation plus all protected route callers remain unverified; plan flags are not license rights.

review_units.label: Packaging
review_units.rationale: The builder configuration names server/UI/plugins/WASM/sidecars/native helper, hardened runtime and external pack/sign hooks. Base notarize:false is not sufficient evidence of the final signed/notarized release; no artifact was built or launched.

review_units.label: License map and reuse inventory
review_units.rationale: REUSE maps general content to MIT and ee to the EE identifier, subject to retained root/EE text, third-party obligations, historical versions and client-side MIT. The report accurately leaves subscription-defined Enterprise Features and exact component clearance unresolved.

review_units.label: Desktop single instance and process ownership
review_units.rationale: The main process requests Electron single-instance lock; registry/recovery queues are process-local. These sources do not establish a lifetime storage lock shared across desktop, CLI/server processes or hosts, and the report does not claim one.

review_units.label: Engine settlement versus deliverable acceptance
review_units.rationale: The success branch exports a transcript and uses final assistant text or a generic fallback, then emits succeeded. That source directly supports the report distinction between engine settlement and independent artifact/test acceptance.

review_units.label: Unexecuted recovery regression cases
review_units.rationale: The retained test definitions cover both generations, lost acknowledgement, manual stop, native recovery, concurrency, policy restoration and retargeted workspaces. Their source is evidence of intended cases only; no execution was performed here.

findings.finding: The phrase non-owner permission reply restrictions is broader than the demonstrated role boundary. Viewers are read-only; collaborators are explicitly allowed to reply to OpenCode permission requests. An owner-only interpretation would contradict the source.
findings.required_change: Say that viewer tokens cannot mutate or approve, while collaborator tokens may answer permission prompts; distinguish host-token/owner-only routes from client proxy routes.
findings.missing_evidence: No additional acquisition is needed for this wording correction. A complete route/actor matrix remains outside this extraction.

findings.finding: The executor awaits input.onAdmitted with worker/workspace/thread/message identity before sendTurn, but the acquired source set contains no implementation of that callback. Awaiting a callback establishes order, not durable persistence or fencing. The report phrase persists ... receipt first overstates what this boundary alone establishes.
findings.required_change: Say that the executor awaits the caller-supplied admission callback before submitting work, and mark its durability/transaction/fencing implementation unverified.
findings.missing_evidence: The production caller in the imported automation service and its receipt-store transaction/identity update path; no such body is present among the 43 captured files.

findings.finding: The helper rejects frames already detached at entry and denied cross-origin delegation, and discards isolated-policy reads when frame origin/URL changes. However, after the final isolated read it returns allowed:true, originKeyed:false when runtime policy is absent/non-origin-keyed. A stale/null isolated result is therefore not itself a blanket denial. The caller that consumes allowed and originKeyed is not retained.
findings.required_change: Limit the statement to the checks actually present, and distinguish a denied frame from allowed but not origin-keyed; do not say every navigated/stale frame fails end-to-end.
findings.missing_evidence: The browser-panel/WebMCP caller and isolated preload implementation, including how both policy flags are consumed and identity is rechecked immediately before execution. This finding is an evidence limit, not a demonstrated runtime exploit.

findings.finding: Six end_line values exceed actual EOF despite quote characters and hashes matching a clamped slice. OW04 points to package lines 79-83, which contain opencode-chrome-devtools but not the claimed @opencode-ai/sdk dependency or compiled plugin build. Those are present at lines 56 and 15 respectively.
findings.required_change: Clamp OW04 to83, OW10 to69, OW18 to7, OW22 to714, OW40 to18 and OW43 to236. Replace or supplement OW04 with exact package line15 build and line56 SDK spans and update its report link.
findings.missing_evidence: None for these corrections; all required text is already retained.

discovery_review.rationale: This is targeted path extraction using a GitHub connector after retained web cache misses. Full connector returns preserve bodies but do not constitute neutral/challenge discovery or per-question screening. The three-batch reference search history is earlier bounded context and does not become a new complete search for these architecture paths. Missing imported evaluator, browser caller, persistence callback and remote provisioning paths are explicit gaps.

lineage_review.rationale: All43 bodies, tests, package declarations and licenses are from one project at one development pin, with inherited identity/license artifacts. Distinct files are complementary primary source context, not independent replication. OpenWork/OpenCode executable integration is now supported by source; installed engine revision and operational correctness remain unverified.

limitations: No new acquisition by this reviewer
No downloaded source, provider, native app or real runtime execution
No overall Helm/Hades enterprise or matched-superiority acceptance
